default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-788.title: Narrowest-bar break
E-788.hypothesis: The narrowest bar of the last n bars marks stalled quoting; the next bar closing beyond its extreme shows which side's resting orders were absorbed; follow.

E-789.title: Stochastic re-entry fade
E-789.hypothesis: A close that leaves the top (bottom) of the recent range marks the end of the push by aggressive buyers (sellers); fade the exit from the extreme zone.

E-790.title: Bar-open gap fade
E-790.hypothesis: A bar opening far from the previous close is a burst of market orders; if the bar then closes back against the burst, the aggressors are underwater; fade the gap.

E-791.title: Rising-volume close stairs
E-791.hypothesis: Consecutive higher closes each on larger volume show participation growing with the move; follow once.

E-792.title: Directional-movement balance cross
E-792.hypothesis: When upward bar extensions dominate downward ones over a window (Wilder directional movement), buyers are repeatedly pushing past prior highs; follow the crossing.

E-793.title: Counter-trend shock bar fade
E-793.hypothesis: In a trending tape a large bar against the trend is often a liquidity sweep by a single large order; trade back with the trend.

E-794.title: End-of-day midpoint pull
E-794.hypothesis: Late in the session, positions are squared toward the day's midpoint; price far from it in the last hour drifts back as day traders close.

E-795.title: Two-bar midpoint reclaim
E-795.hypothesis: After a large bar, an opposite bar that retakes more than half of its body without exceeding its open shows the first move was rejected; trade the rejection.

E-796.title: Volume dry-up then expansion
E-796.hypothesis: Three bars of very thin volume mean the book was left alone; the first bar with heavy volume shows the side that finally acts; follow its colour.

E-797.title: Regression slope threshold cross
E-797.hypothesis: A least-squares line through recent closes that becomes steep enough shows persistent one-sided pressure rather than one noisy spike; follow the crossing.
